title: Reverse Grip
text: “If I remember Motoyasu-kun’s account correctly, Raphtalia-chan, Larsazusa-san, and Sakura-chan ended up as holders of the hammer among the Seven Star Weapons, right?”
“Naofumi got close to her with the aim of recruiting Larsazusa as a candidate holder, and that’s how Sadeena ended up tagging along.”
“Ah, brings back memories. Turned out well in the end, didn’t it? Though at that time Larsazusa-san was a claw hero candidate.”
“In a different loop she ends up as the hammer’s holder instead.”

“Honestly, I think Larsazusa-san’s grandfather would’ve been more suited to being the holder. Wasn’t there a story about how Larsazusa-san got worked to the bone by her grandfather in that particular loop?”
Father asked me directly, so I nodded, I say.
“Indeed.”
“Want to give it a try?”

Thanks to the reincarnators popping up one after another in turn, the Seven Star Weapons had stopped responding altogether in this particular loop. At least it was some small mercy that Rival hadn’t become the claw hero this time around. Though now that I thought about it… once Rival did become a hero, it apparently persuaded the claw’s Seven Star Weapon into cooperating without much trouble. Exactly how it managed to persuade the thing remained a genuine mystery to me, I say.
“Might be worth testing once we get back home. Motoyasu-kun and the others can vouch for it too, after all…”
“Though honestly, the world isn’t exactly in crisis anymore, is it? You could argue there’s no real need for new heroes at this point.”
“Yeah, that’s true… The heroes just being Motoyasu-kun and the rest of us handled everything just fine.”

Indeed. This particular world had turned out remarkably well, I say. Aside from the massive damage Melromarc suffered under the Three Heroes Church and the vengeful spirit of the Crimson Swine after we took down Trash, that is. As a result, the loop had apparently triggered right at the moment I died in the very first world. Since this was the continuation of that timeline, the world at large had settled into peace.
“Something’s been bugging me a little — hypothetically, if the heroes of the Seven Star Weapons ended up in the same situation as us, what would happen, do you think?”
“Assuming the whole turning-into-frontier-animals thing is tied specifically to being a hero, then by that logic the hammer hero would turn into a Peckul…”
“So Raphtalia-chan, Larsazusa-san, and Sakura-chan would all become Peckuls?”
“Our numbers would grow, Naofumi-san.”
“Raphtalia-chan I can sort of picture, but Larsazusa-san and Sakura-chan already have other transformed forms — would they turn into Peckuls on top of that?”

Transforming into yet another different form, I say. It brought to mind the image of Big Sister holding a hammer in her Raph-species form. Would that become a Peckul form too? That seemed like it would only add to the confusion, I say. How would Father react upon reuniting with the Father from the first world, or with Fleon-chan? Big Sister transformed into a Peckul… somehow I could easily picture Father cradling and petting her. And what if Father himself turned into a Peckul in the process? Whether Father would still get petted in that case, I honestly couldn’t say. Confusion would certainly follow, I say.
“I suppose it should be viewed as a kind of status ailment. Still, I’m a little curious about it.”
“Even if Sakura became a Peckul, I doubt it’d feel that out of place. At most the size would change.”
“And what exactly is that supposed to mean? Do you have some kind of complaint about Sakura-chan?”
Ren was throwing shade at the idea of Sakura-chan turning into a Peckul, I say. Filolial-sama and Peckul are entirely different things, I say.
“Well, they’re both birds, and neither can fly, so there’s plenty of overlap.”

Come to think of it, there was that time Filo-tan showed up at Cal Mira Island in Peckul colors. If I recalled correctly, wearing the costume temporarily shifted her coloring that way. She’d still looked like Filolial-sama, but somehow also like a Peckul at the same time.
“With Sakura-san, I’m fairly certain it’d just end up being cute and nothing more — no real trouble to speak of. If anything, it might end up delaying the resolution of whatever problem’s at hand.”
“She’s the easygoing type, after all. I can just picture her going ‘not really bothered by it’…”
Since Peckul is essentially Father, this would only add to the sense of parent-and-child, I say. Which meant Filo-tan too, by extension, was a Peckul.
“I’d like to become a Peckul myself, I say.”
“Wh— Motoyasu-kun just came out of nowhere with something bizarre again!?”
“You’re a Usaunny, aren’t you.”
“Since they all seem to differ as if by prior arrangement, I can’t really tell if it’s determined weapon by weapon.”
“Well… at the very least, it’s a relief this status ailment doesn’t seem to be contagious, right?”

“Naofumi-san, that’s not really something to joke about. If it were contagious, I’d probably be the first one spreading it around, wouldn’t I? Going around saying ‘sorry, I refuse to be the only Riska here’ and turning everyone else into one too.”
“Aren’t you being a little too hard on yourself? Even Itsuki wouldn’t go that far, surely.”
“All of humanity, all living things turning into frontier animals, huh… in a way, that might actually be peaceful.”
Frontier animals as far as the eye could see, I say. A world where Filo-tan, Filolial-sama, and every single person I knew in this world ceased to be human.
“No, no, hold on…”
“Maybe once we clear this dungeon, some spell like that gets cast on the whole world.”

Ren muttered it like it was just a joke. Itsuki looked like he was about to say something, then clapped a hand over his own mouth and glanced toward Father instead — probably wary of accidentally triggering something with a stray hit.
“I’ll just abandon that line of thought entirely. If I think about it wrong and it somehow comes true, that’d be a nightmare.”
“Ren, could you not? That’s really not a joking matter. We set out to solve things, and now there’s a chance we end up plunging the world into chaos instead.”
“But can you really say for certain there’s no such possibility? Every one of us besides Naofumi got fooled by our game knowledge, remember.”

“I can’t say for sure there’s no game out there designed to mislead players like that, so I can’t rule it out entirely — but all we can do is keep going and hope it isn’t that. We do need to get back to normal, after all.”
Quite right, I say. We’d come to investigate Cal Mira Island and entered this dungeon precisely in order to return to our original forms.
“Well… anyway, something occurred to me — among the future tools Rafuemon and the others have, is there perhaps some device that could restore us… return us to our past forms?”
“Well… going by where the ideas seem to originate from, it wouldn’t be surprising if something like that existed. But you haven’t heard of anything like that, have you, Itsuki?”
Father made some gesture like spreading out a cloth.
“That does seem to be the case. Rafuemon-san tends to overlook things, so I asked Filoko-san and Rafumi-san as well.”
Ren crossed his arms, brow furrowed, seemingly turning the matter over in his mind.
“Those guys seemed to have some vague idea of what happens in the future. No question they’re hiding something.”
“So they know a way back but deliberately kept quiet about it… Looks like the world’s heading for a frontier-animal ending after all.”
“That might just be the worst possible future imaginable…”
“You’re overthinking it. There’s no character out there trying to mislead us, so it’s probably fine.”
“I wonder about that. Either way, it seems all we can do is keep moving forward.”
With that worry weighing on our chests, we pressed onward.
“Air Strike Bash X!”

For some reason, Ren unleashed the skill on the monster that appeared by holding his sword in a reverse grip and swinging it upward, I say. As for skills, they can apparently be released with a fair amount of freedom in bodily motion.
“Ren, are you getting bored fighting monsters along the way? Are you just messing around?”
“Yeah, I’m messing around.”
“Said it without a shred of shame. Is that also a chuunibyou thing? Some kind of self-styled swordsmanship?”
“There was a technique like that in a manga I used to read. An old classic battle manga, actually.”
Father answered as though sinking into nostalgia, I say. So such battle manga existed, I say.
“An impression of it, perhaps?”
“Does something like that actually exist?”
“You don’t know it, Ren-san? Then maybe it was something someone online was doing.”

“There’s a style where you use techniques meant for daggers with a longsword instead. The handling’s got its quirks, but battle-maniac types called it a ‘strash,’ though I never quite got the reasoning behind it…”

“I’ve heard it’s a coined term — originally combining ‘straight,’ as in a straight cut, with ‘slash.’ Though I’ve also heard another theory that it’s ‘strike’ plus ‘slash.’ So something like that exists in your world too, Ren.”
“Huh…”
“There are combo skills too, right? Why not try one out as a test?”

Come to think of it, there’d been that story about Father using a combo skill when he borrowed a staff from Trash. It had been a skill related to the Float Shield, reflecting an attack countless times to form something like a cage. Something called Blast Prison, if I recalled — depending on the combination, skills could apparently merge into entirely different ones altogether.
